$comment: Semantic intents registry (v3) — copy to ~/.iphone-use/intents-registry.json and curate. This file, not the phone, is the capability list: POST /agent/intent only dispatches verbs listed here, GET /agent/intents serves it verbatim. Adding a verb is a reviewed change (add the branch to the bridge shortcut AND the entry here); agents never create shortcuts at runtime. The daemon opens shortcuts://run-shortcut?name=<bridge>&input=text&text=<urlencoded {verb,id,args}> on-device via WDA POST /url; the bridge shortcut POSTs {id,verb,ok,data} back to /agent/inbox with the bearer token + X-Phone-Control: 1. First run of each privacy-sensitive verb (and the first POST to the daemon host) needs one interactive permission tap on the phone — run each verb once by hand after installing the bridge. The Shortcuts app foregrounds for the duration of every run.

bridge.$comment: The ONE reviewed bridge shortcut. It takes its JSON request from Shortcut Input (input=text), dispatches on `verb`, runs the native action, and POSTs the result to /agent/inbox. Keep the bearer token only inside the shortcut's stored request headers — it must never appear in the deep link.
bridge.name: iU Bridge

intents.$comment: Mandatory liveness verb: zero permissions, returns the installed bridge version. A ping round trip is the only real proof the bridge is installed and current.
intents.name: ping

intents.$comment: Read-only example verb; validated the legacy round trip. side_effect none|read verbs are safe to re-dispatch after outcome not_sent; write verbs are never blindly replayed.
intents.name: battery
